Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. President Trump is in South Carolina
to support Republican Senator Darlene Graham, who's in a tough campaign against Democratic
nominee Annie Andrews. Graham replaced her late brother Lindsey Graham in the Senate.
More than $34 million has flowed into the race. Republicans call Andrews a radical liberal,
which she denies. Andrews criticizes Darlene Graham's inexperience.
President Trump says the U.S. gave Russia nothing in exchange for releasing Stephen
Hubbard. NPR's Franco Ordonez reports the Michigan teacher had been held since the early
days of Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
President Trump says he asked Putin to release Hubbard during talks about ending the war
in Ukraine.
I hear he's in pretty good shape. He went through a lot. I spoke to him this morning.
He is the happiest man around. He didn't think this was going to be. This was very surprising
to him, but I did it. It really took place on a phone call at the end of last week with
President Putin, so we appreciate it very much.
Trump says his administration did not offer Russia anything in return, even criticizing
past negotiations for he claims giving money. But earlier this month, Trump announced he
struck a deal to purchase diesel fuel for Russia and then waived major sanctions that
target Russian officials, banks and the energy sector. Franco Ordonez, NPR News, the White
House.
The Supreme Court has ruled that the Trump administration must continue to provide gender-affirming
care to transgender inmates. NPR's Jacqueline Diaz has more.
The Supreme Court's decision upholds a lower court's injunction on a federal Bureau of
Prisons policy that would terminate hormone therapy and other treatments for trans inmates.
The court offered no explanation for the decision. As a lower court's injunction remains in place,
the litigation over the policy continues. The American Civil Liberties Union sued the
Trump administration over its proposed policy. The organization believes there are more than
2,000 people in federal custody who identify as transgender and could be impacted by any
future policy changes. Jacqueline Diaz, NPR News.
A new report finds nearly nine out of 10 U.S. school districts have not recovered from the
pandemic and have declining student math and reading scores. NPR's Janaki Mehta reports.
Even though student achievement in math and reading have been suffering since 2013, things
have only gotten worse since the pandemic. The new report found that only 13 states have
a clear, specific statewide goal for student learning, like South Carolina, which aims
for 75 percent of its students to be performing at grade level by 2030. 43 states have passed
legislation on quality reading instruction, but only 18 states have done so for math.
The most aggressive policies are in Republican-led states, but overall far fewer states have
schools that are actually putting what's in the law into practice in the classroom.
Janaki Mehta, NPR News.
And from Washington, you're listening to NPR News.
California state workers began a one-day strike today, urging Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom
to agree to a new labor contract. The union wants the state to raise workers' salaries
by 20 percent over the next three years and increase the state contribution toward employees'
health care costs. And members oppose a mandate by Newsom requiring state workers to report
to the office four days a week. It could be a good night for wishing on a star tonight.
The Orionids meteor shower is expected to be in peak view, displaying shooting stars
against a backdrop of totally dark skies, but only after the moon sets. NPR's Mikayla
Gray has more.
NASA says the Orionids shower is viewable both in the northern and southern hemispheres.
The meteor shower is known for its brightness and speed, and Halley's comet is what produces
the icy and rocky dust that forms the spectacle. It'll be visible across the U.S. overnight,
but it's best viewed under certain conditions. Through much of the night, the moon will wash
over all but the brightest shooting stars. For night owls and very early risers, NASA
suggests watching in a location away from city lights and lying down while looking up
at clear, dark skies. Your eyes may need 30 minutes to adjust.
The Orionids are on display every October. While at its peak now, the meteor shower will
be active until November 7th. Mikayla Gray, NPR News.
Villanova and Notre Dame's men's and women's teams are set to play a double-header in Rome
on November 1st, marking the start of the college basketball season. The Eternal City
Tip-Off celebrates the Catholic University's shared mission, and Villanova alum Pope Leo
is scheduled to hold a private audience with the teams.
I'm Rylan Barton. This is NPR News.
